taxonomy.subtopic: Respiratory ventricular interdependence and pulsus paradoxus

questions.stem_html: A 45-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer develops dyspnea, tachycardia, hypotension, and distended neck veins. An arterial catheter tracing is shown. During inspiration, systolic pressure repeatedly falls by 14 mm Hg. Which mechanism most directly produces this finding?

options.text_html: Inspiration directly reduces myocardial contractility through vagal activation
Inspiratory pulmonary vasoconstriction abruptly increases left ventricular afterload
Expiration increases right ventricular preload and compresses the left ventricle
Inspiratory collapse of the inferior vena cava prevents right ventricular filling
Inspiratory expansion of the right ventricle within a fixed pericardial volume shifts the septum leftward and reduces left ventricular filling

questions.explanation_html: In tamponade, elevated intrapericardial pressure restricts total cardiac volume. Inspiration increases systemic venous return to the right heart. Because the ventricles cannot expand outward, the right ventricle enlarges at the expense of the left ventricle, shifting the septum leftward. Left ventricular filling and stroke volume fall excessively during inspiration, causing pulsus paradoxus.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: The key abnormality is ventricular interdependence in a constrained pericardial space, not abrupt pulmonary vasoconstriction.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: Right ventricular filling increases during inspiration, not expiration.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: The beat-to-beat pressure change is mechanical and preload-related rather than direct vagal depression of contractility.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Impaired right-sided filling results from pericardial pressure, not inspiratory caval collapse.

questions.educational_objective: Cardiac tamponade exaggerates ventricular interdependence: inspiratory right ventricular filling displaces the septum leftward and lowers left ventricular preload and systolic pressure.
